provenance.orgName: Cirencester, Gloucestershire. Augustinian abbey of St Mary the Virgin
provenance.p: Two Cirencester scribes have been identified as having written the book, one of whom is identifiable as Master Walter. See M. Gullick, 'A twelfth-century manuscript of the letters of Thomas Becket', English Manuscript Studies 1100–1700 2 (1990), 1–31. For the textual importance of the manuscript, see also A. Duggan, The Correspondence of Thomas Becket, Archbishop of Canterbury, 1162–1170, OMT (2000), lxxxiv-xciii.

provenance.orgName: Canterbury, Kent. Benedictine cathedral priory of Holy Trinity or Christ Church
provenance.p: Rejected in the Supplement: "Widely accepted as a Canterbury book, this must now be ascribed to Cirencester because of Mr Michael Gullick's discovery (communicated by letter) that the principal scribe is the Cirencester scribe Walter, who wrote London, British Library, MS Royal 7 B. vi, and that it bears annotations by Alexander Nequam, canon of Cirencester (BRUO)."

Cotton MS Claudius B. ii was "included in the index to the 1963 edn. as from Canterbury but by an oversight omitted from the text" (as explained retrospectively in the 1987 Supplement, p. 12, n. 1). The corresponding index card originally recorded the following information (now superseded): 2o folio: dabat memoria. Hand beginning at fol. 139v is very handsome and uses 7 and biting of d with e: it goes to fol. 141v. Reference in the form in alio libro, fol. 206: In alio libro hic habetur epistola que est supra xxxiii.... Probability that this is a Christ Church book.

recordHist.source: Neil R. Ker, ed., Medieval Libraries of Great Britain: A List of Surviving Books, Royal Historical Society Guides and Handbooks, 3 (London, 1941; 2nd edn, 1964; supplement, ed. Andrew G. Watson, 1987; digital edn, ed. Richard Sharpe and James M. W. Willoughby, 2010–15).

revisionDesc.change: Record 1240 merged into this record. Record updated to reflect the changes introduced in the 1987 supplement, in which the Canterbury attribution was revisited and rejected.
